expected_items.description: Interpret the user's Timekeeper request as a reusable platform agent for deadlines, duration, and hurry-up pressure.
expected_items.rationale: The request was summarized and the plan records the Timekeeper agent interpretation.

expected_items.description: Run web-first research and save a public search record.
expected_items.rationale: The search record lists queries, sources checked, plan impact, and uncertainty.

expected_items.description: Add or link the durable requirement for the Timekeeper agent.
Create an inspectable agent spec with deadline, timebox, critical path, and hurry-up trade-off policy.
expected_items.rationale: The agent spec includes trigger, input schema, output contract, urgency levels, safety rules, and validation commands.

expected_items.description: Reuse the existing work-timer rather than creating a duplicate timing tool.
expected_items.rationale: The agent links the work-timer policy, and the timing record validates with the work-timer.

expected_items.description: Ensure urgency does not bypass required verification or safety gates.
expected_items.rationale: The policy states urgency is not permission to skip checks and should alter scope, sequence, parallelism, or checkpoint cadence.

acceptance_checks.description: Confirm the new agent appears in the registry list.
Run platform tests and monitor build checks.
acceptance_checks.rationale: All commands completed with exit code 0.

known_omission_risks: Reminder cadence and actual notification channel are intentionally not configured because the user did not specify them and no token/webhook should be assumed.
notes: No new timing runtime, calendar integration, or real notification delivery was implemented.
